title: Independent families: freely choosing sides and counting ultrafilters

based_on.title: Set Theory: The Third Millennium Edition, revised and expanded

summary: Continuum many subsets can realize every finite pattern of choices, giving the largest possible number of nonprincipal ultrafilters.
abstract: For a family of subsets of the natural numbers, choosing some sets and the complements of others imposes membership requirements. Call the family independent when every finite pattern of these choices is satisfied by infinitely many natural numbers. Such a family can have as many members as there are real numbers. Assuming the axiom of choice, every assignment of sides to all its members extends to a nonprincipal ultrafilter, a consistent way to declare exactly one side of every complementary pair large. Different assignments give different ultrafilters, yielding as many nonprincipal ultrafilters as there are families of subsets of the natural numbers.
